reviewer_lens: Own-Policy-Adherence: Dependency. Cross-product refusal (lean-a2), substrate DAG acyclicity (ADR-0280), no-cycles validated, vendor lock-in avoidance (ADR-0173), direction-of-dependency rules (lean-a1).
verdict_summary: The bundle's dependency doctrine is conceptually sound and well-grounded in industry precedent (Hamilton LISA 2007, Bezos API mandate, Borg/K8s strata, Stripe tier model). ADR-0280's DAG schema, twelve dependency rules, Markov-chain SLO composition, per-edge cascade rules, forbidden-edge negative-space assertions, build-time procedural macro, and chaos-drill cadence are all correctly framed and create a defensible single-source-of-truth surface. ADR-0173 and ADR-0211 together correctly capture vendor lock-in posture (Tier-I/II/III + Class-A/B/C) and align on owning-the-stack via OSS substrate. HOWEVER, three load-bearing artifacts that the doctrine declares are MISSING from the workspace and convert the doctrine from 'enforceable' to 'aspirational' on day-1: (a) specs/substrate-dependency-dag.json does not exist, (b) specs/microservice-dependency-dag.json (ADR-0245 forward-declared, ADR-0280 §Alt-5 'Resolved — adopt both') does not exist, (c) no oya-check-substrate-dependency-dag-acyclicity validator crate exists in crates/. ADR-0280 self-classifies as 'advisory-until-dag-spec-lands-and-validator-green', so the missing artifacts are scoped to the post-acceptance landing wave per its own §Status — this is why the verdict is CONDITIONAL-APPROVE rather than REJECT. The conditions are concrete and tracked below.

dag_cycles_detected.method: manual trace of the 45 edges declared in ADR-0280 §D-1 example payload
dag_cycles_detected.evidence: All declared edges respect bootstrap_order positions (cell < identity < tenancy < policy-engine < cloud-secrets < audit-chain < observability < ontology < intelligence < workflow-engine). No edge in the worked example points from a lower-bootstrap-position node back to a higher-bootstrap-position node. The 22 forbidden-edges_assertion entries correctly enumerate the negative-space cycle-introducing edges (e.g., policy-engine→ontology, ontology→intelligence, audit-chain→workflow-engine).
dag_cycles_detected.residual_risk: Without specs/substrate-dependency-dag.json + Tarjan validator landed, future PRs CAN silently introduce a backward edge. PR #143 close-out audit (cited in ADR-0280 §Context 'Why now') already flagged two near-misses where a substrate accidentally imported a higher substrate's client crate at refactor time — exactly the failure mode this doctrine exists to close.

dag_cycles_detected.method: review of Rule R-5 (cloud-secrets follows policy-engine at runtime)
dag_cycles_detected.evidence: ADR-0280 §D-2 R-5 says cloud-secrets is bootstrap-step-3 (before identity) but at RUNTIME depends only on cell — identity/tenancy/policy-engine call cloud-secrets, not the reverse. The DAG schema's 'bootstrap_seam' field (referenced in §D-2 R-2 and R-5) is mentioned but is NOT defined in the §D-1 JSON schema. This is a schema gap that could allow a contributor to encode the bootstrap-only seam as either (a) a runtime edge (which would reintroduce a cycle: cloud-secrets→identity AND identity→cloud-secrets via implicit reverse use) or (b) an undeclared invariant (which the validator cannot enforce).
dag_cycles_detected.residual_risk: Schema in §D-1 must be amended to add the optional 'bootstrap_seams: [{from, to, phase: 'bootstrap-only'}]' surface, with the acyclicity validator excluding bootstrap-only seams from Tarjan SCC computation but still emitting them in evidence.

dag_cycles_detected.method: cross-check ADR-0245 §D (line 660-670) declared substrate ordering vs ADR-0280 §D-2 ordering
dag_cycles_detected.evidence: ADR-0245 line 662-670 declares: 'policy-engine (depends on tenancy + identity + audit-chain + observability)'. ADR-0280 declares policy-engine depends ONLY on cell+identity+tenancy and that audit-chain DEPENDS ON policy-engine (forbidden_edges_assertion explicitly lists policy-engine→audit-chain as forbidden). ADR-0245 is the older prose; ADR-0280 amends it per its §Header amends list. But ADR-0245's text is not yet updated in this bundle. This is a documentation drift, not a code-level cycle, BUT a contributor reading ADR-0245 alone could mis-author the manifest.
dag_cycles_detected.residual_risk: MEDIUM. ADR-0245 §D text needs a stub amendment ('see ADR-0280 §D-1 for the canonical dependency direction; the dependency lines in §D below are superseded') or the bundle is internally inconsistent on its load-bearing topology declaration.

cross_product_violations.rule: lean-a2 cross-product refusal (products call each other ONLY through Workflow + Ontology adapter layer)
cross_product_violations.scope_of_bundle: The keystone bundle is substrate-layer doctrine; products are out of bundle scope per ADR-0245 substrate-vs-product layering. ADR-0280 explicitly scopes to substrate-to-substrate dependency direction.
cross_product_violations.note: Bundle correctly stays in the substrate lane. No new product-to-product edges introduced. The DAG schema does NOT allow product nodes, which is the right scoping.

cross_product_violations.rule: Adapter trait + multi-impl requirement (ADR-0173 D-Seam, ADR-0083 port-in-kernel)
cross_product_violations.scope_of_bundle: ADR-0280 §D-10 build-time DAG check via procedural macro IS an adapter-trait pattern over the spec file.
cross_product_violations.note: The oya-shared-<substrate>-client-{kernel, adapter, sdk} family naming declared in ADR-0246 §D-3 and consumed by ADR-0280 §D-10 satisfies the port-in-kernel + adapter pattern. assert_dag_edge! macro is the build-time enforcement seam.

cross_product_violations.rule: Direction-of-dependency rule (lean-a1) — substrate depends on substrate only; never on product
cross_product_violations.note: ADR-0280 §D-1 schema's tier_subtype enum is 'substrate-*' only; products cannot register as DAG nodes. This is structural enforcement, not just doctrinal.

cross_product_violations.rule: Workflow + Ontology as the universal adapter layer for cross-product calls
cross_product_violations.scope_of_bundle: Workflow-engine (substrate-orchestration) and Ontology (substrate-data) both appear in the DAG. workflow-engine has an outgoing edge to ontology (weight 0.7, DEGRADED).
cross_product_violations.note: The substrate-level realization of the adapter doctrine is preserved. Products will reach across each other via these two substrates, not directly. ADR-0145 invariants 1+2 (direct gRPC permitted between substrates) is correctly scoped to substrates only, not products.

vendor_lock_in_concerns.finding: ADR-0211 (Class A/B/C) and ADR-0173 (Tier I/II/III) use DIFFERENT taxonomies for the SAME concept. ADR-0211 Class A ≈ ADR-0173 Tier I (community-standard KEEP/OWNED). ADR-0211 Class B ≈ ADR-0173 Tier II (vendor-seamed, Phase-2 native). ADR-0211 Class C ≈ ADR-0173 — partial overlap. ADR-0173 Tier III (FORBIDDEN) maps to nothing in ADR-0211; ADR-0211 Class C (in-house mandatory differentiation) maps to nothing in ADR-0173.
vendor_lock_in_concerns.recommendation: Bundle should add a §Crosswalk-Appendix to one of the two ADRs (preferably ADR-0211 since it post-dates ADR-0173) declaring the mapping table. The CI gate oya-check-vendor-classification-coverage (declared in ADR-0211 §CI-enforcement) must validate EITHER taxonomy; a contributor today could mis-classify by reading only one ADR.

vendor_lock_in_concerns.concern: Cedar declared 'community standard' (ADR-0211 Class A) but is AWS-stewarded
vendor_lock_in_concerns.finding: ADR-0211 lists Cedar as Class A (community-standard KEEP). ADR-0173 Tier I notes 'Cedar (v4.2) — Apache-2.0, AWS-stewarded, spec stable; ADR-0007 cedar authorization. Bus-factor mitigated by spec stability and active community engine forks.' The bus-factor concern is acknowledged but the per-edge dependency in ADR-0280 (every cross-substrate call passes through Cedar via policy-engine) gives Cedar an extremely heavy structural dependency weight.
vendor_lock_in_concerns.recommendation: Concentration risk is documented but not quantified. ADR-0280 §D-7 Cedar permit fragments are tightly coupled to Cedar's policy language; a Cedar replacement would require re-authoring every per-edge fragment. ADR-0280 should explicitly note in §Consequences-Negative that Cedar replacement is BLOCKED by per-edge fragment author cost — escalating the Cedar dependency from Class-A 'fine' to 'we now own this risk forever'. Acceptable if explicit; problematic if hidden.

vendor_lock_in_concerns.finding: ADR-0280 places cloud-secrets at Tier-1 with SLO floor 0.99995 and T0 DR tier. ADR-0173 Tier I lists OpenBao as the substrate. OpenBao is a fork (MPL-2.0) of HashiCorp Vault post-BUSL pivot. The dependency on OpenBao's continued community vitality is load-bearing for the entire DAG.
vendor_lock_in_concerns.recommendation: ADR-0211 should add a phase-2 contingency: if OpenBao community vitality drops below an explicit signal (commit frequency, security-CVE response time), trigger an oya-cloud-secrets in-house path. Today no signal is defined; OpenBao is treated as permanently safe.

vendor_lock_in_concerns.concern: Intelligence substrate provider list (Anthropic + OpenAI + Gemini) all are Tier II vendor-seamed
vendor_lock_in_concerns.finding: ADR-0280 places intelligence at Tier-1 SLO 0.999. ADR-0173 Tier II lists all three LLM providers. ADR-0026 in-house model substrate is the replacement target but no quantified readiness gate beyond 'human-eval >= 95% + tool-use parity'.
vendor_lock_in_concerns.recommendation: Not blocking; ADR-0173's seam-and-multi-impl pattern (6 adapter crates) is already in place. But the dependency-weight 0.5 (DEGRADED) on workflow-engine→intelligence in ADR-0280 §D-1 example is well-chosen — intelligence brown-out does NOT kill workflow-engine. This is correct.

vendor_lock_in_concerns.concern: vendor-lockin-discipline gate is declared BLOCKER but does NOT include substrate-DAG-acyclicity
vendor_lock_in_concerns.finding: ADR-0173 §CI-lane lists 'oya gate validate vendor-lockin-discipline' which checks vendor registry entries — NOT DAG acyclicity. ADR-0280 §D-3 declares 'oya-check-substrate-dependency-dag-acyclicity' as a separate lane. These are two enforcement surfaces. A contributor could ADD a vendor (passing vendor-lockin-discipline) that introduces a DAG cycle (failing DAG acyclicity). Today, neither gate is wired (vendor-lockin-discipline crate exists; substrate-DAG-acyclicity crate does NOT).
vendor_lock_in_concerns.recommendation: MUST land BEFORE bundle is promoted from 'advisory' to BLOCKER. The crate oya-check-substrate-dependency-dag-acyclicity must exist with green tests.

top_findings.finding: specs/substrate-dependency-dag.json does NOT exist. ADR-0280's enforcement_status field correctly self-classifies as 'advisory-until-dag-spec-lands-and-validator-green', so this is on the critical path for promotion to BLOCKER, not for ADR acceptance. But the bundle's load-bearing artifact is missing from the workspace.
top_findings.remediation: Land the JSON spec file with the v1.0.0 content from ADR-0280 §D-1 worked example as the initial payload. Land alongside the oya-check-substrate-dependency-dag-acyclicity validator crate.

top_findings.finding: ADR-0280 §D-1 JSON schema does NOT define the 'bootstrap_seam' field referenced in Rules R-2 and R-5. Without explicit schema support, the bootstrap-only seam between cloud-secrets and identity (Shamir-shared genesis) is undeclared and could either be encoded as a runtime edge (creating a cycle) or not encoded at all (lost institutional knowledge).
top_findings.remediation: Amend ADR-0280 §D-1 schema to add optional 'bootstrap_seams' array with {from, to, phase: 'bootstrap-only', reason} entries. Tarjan validator MUST exclude bootstrap_seams from SCC computation but include them in catalog rendering.
top_findings.evidence_path: ADR-0280:768 (R-2 bootstrap-only seam reference); ADR-0280:782 (R-5 cloud-secrets runtime vs bootstrap inversion); ADR-0280:359-431 (§D-1 schema; field missing)

top_findings.finding: ADR-0245 §D (line 662-670) declares an older dependency order ('policy-engine depends on tenancy + identity + audit-chain + observability') that contradicts ADR-0280's authoritative DAG (policy-engine depends ONLY on cell+identity+tenancy; audit-chain depends on policy-engine, not the reverse). The bundle does not amend ADR-0245's prose; ADR-0280's amends-list says it 'hardens §D-4 dependency-direction text' but the §D body of ADR-0245 remains misleading.
top_findings.remediation: Add a stub note in ADR-0245 §D pointing readers to ADR-0280 §D-1 as canonical, OR explicitly amend ADR-0245's listed substrate dependencies to match ADR-0280's DAG. Bundle must not ship with contradictory canonical references.

top_findings.finding: ADR-0211 Class A/B/C and ADR-0173 Tier I/II/III are two taxonomies for the same concept. Cross-walk is implied but not declared. A contributor following ADR-0211 alone won't know about the Tier III FORBIDDEN list in ADR-0173.
top_findings.remediation: Add a Crosswalk appendix to ADR-0211 explicitly mapping Class A/B/C ↔ Tier I/II/III and noting that Tier III FORBIDDEN has no Class equivalent (which means Class system is silently more permissive than Tier system — a doctrinal gap).

top_findings.finding: ADR-0280 §Alt-5 'Resolved — adopt both' commits to TWO DAG specs: specs/substrate-dependency-dag.json AND specs/microservice-dependency-dag.json. The latter is forward-declared by ADR-0245 but neither file exists. The lane 'oya-check-substrate-dag-subset-of-microservice-dag' is mentioned but no crate is registered for it.
top_findings.remediation: Either land both specs OR amend ADR-0280 §Alt-5 to consolidate into one spec (substrate is subset of microservice DAG — the broader DAG could be a superset view rendered from manifest dependencies). The bundle as authored requires TWO files that both don't exist.

top_findings.finding: ADR-0280 §Rule R-11 declares Foundry as Tier-S5 substrate-meta, depending on every other substrate. ADR-0247 self-hosting doctrine commits Foundry to USING the platform's substrates. This means Foundry's bootstrap depends on the substrates being up; but the substrates' CI/migration is RUN BY Foundry. This is a bootstrap-time cycle that v1.0.0 of the DAG correctly excludes (Foundry is in Appendix C, lands in v1.2.0).
top_findings.remediation: Bundle correctly defers. When Foundry lands in v1.2.0, the bootstrap-time cycle MUST be encoded as bootstrap_seam (per finding rank-2 above), not as runtime edge. Pre-document the seam now to avoid v1.2.0 cycle introduction.
top_findings.evidence_path: ADR-0280:828-833 (Rule R-11); ADR-0280:2215-2219 (Appendix C Tier-S5); ADR-0247 (self-hosting doctrine)

top_findings.finding: Every cross-substrate edge in ADR-0280 §D-1 carries a 'cedar_permit_fragment' attribute. This makes Cedar a single-point-of-substitution-cost across the entire substrate dependency graph. Per ADR-0211, Cedar is Class A (KEEP indefinitely); per ADR-0173, Cedar is Tier I 'with asterisk' (AWS-stewarded). The escalation from 'keep' to 'irreplaceable' is implicit.
top_findings.remediation: ADR-0280 §Consequences-Negative should explicitly call out Cedar concentration: 'Replacing Cedar requires re-authoring 45+ per-edge permit fragments. This makes Cedar an effectively-permanent dependency at Tier-1 substrate scale; future replacement requires its own substrate-rebuild ADR.' Today the cost is hidden.
top_findings.evidence_path: ADR-0280:399 (cedar_permit_fragment required per edge); ADR-0173:117-119 (Cedar bus-factor)

positive_findings: ADR-0280's twelve dependency rules (R-1..R-12) are well-structured and externally grounded (Hamilton LISA 2007 §2.2, Borg/K8s stratification, Bezos API mandate, Stripe tier model, AWS Builders' Library). Pattern attribution table (Appendix A) is exemplary.

Forbidden-edges_assertion (negative-space declaration) is a strong invariant — most DAG systems only declare positive edges. The 22 explicit forbidden edges close the silent-cycle-introduction class of bugs at schema level.
Build-time procedural macro (§D-10 assert_dag_edge!) catches DAG violations at cargo check time rather than CI time — short feedback loop.
Per-edge cascade_rule (FULL/DEGRADED/BROWNOUT/INDEPENDENT) is operationally precise — gives on-call responders a deterministic answer to 'when X is down, what happens to Y'.
SLO composition formula (§D-6) is mathematically explicit (Markov-chain product) and bounded — substrates cannot over-promise SLOs that their dependencies cannot deliver.

ADR-0173 + ADR-0211 together cover both the doctrinal posture (own-the-stack default) AND the per-vendor inventory (registry/vendor-lockin-phaseout/index.json) AND the CI enforcement (oya-check-vendor-lockin-discipline). Three-layer defense-in-depth.
Cedar permit fragment naming convention (permit-<from>-call-<to>-v<N>) is mechanically generable from the DAG — eliminates author-by-hand coverage gaps that PR #143 review evidence flagged.
approval_conditions_for_BLOCKER_promotio: C1: specs/substrate-dependency-dag.json lands at workspace root with the v1.0.0 payload from ADR-0280 §D-1.
C2: crates/oya-check-substrate-dependency-dag-acyclicity-* lands, compiles, exits 0 on the v1.0.0 payload, and exits 1 on synthetic cycle fixtures in tests/fixtures/dag-cycles/.
C3: ADR-0280 §D-1 JSON schema amended to add 'bootstrap_seams' field for bootstrap-only seams (closes Finding-Rank-2).
C4: ADR-0245 §D substrate dependency text either superseded-pointer-to-ADR-0280 OR amended to match ADR-0280 §D-1 (closes Finding-Rank-3).
C5: ADR-0211 §Crosswalk appendix added mapping Class A/B/C ↔ Tier I/II/III (closes Finding-Rank-4).
C6: Decision on Alt-5 dual-DAG: either land both specs OR consolidate to one (closes Finding-Rank-5).
C7: Cedar concentration risk explicitly called out in ADR-0280 §Consequences-Negative (closes Finding-Rank-7).
verdict_rationale: The dependency doctrine is structurally correct, internally consistent in its core (12 rules + 22 forbidden edges + Markov-chain SLO composition + per-edge cascade rules + build-time macro + chaos-drill cadence), and well-grounded in named industry precedent. The vendor lock-in posture (ADR-0173 + ADR-0211) is also well-formed though taxonomy-fragmented. The bundle correctly self-classifies enforcement as advisory pending the dependency artifacts landing. CONDITIONAL-APPROVE rather than full APPROVE because the 7 conditions above are concrete and must land before the doctrine becomes enforceable. No condition blocks ADR ACCEPTANCE; all conditions block ADR PROMOTION to BLOCKER status. No cycles detected in the declared edges. No cross-product violations detected. No vendor lock-in blocking concerns detected — concentrations (Cedar, OpenBao) are documented though under-quantified.

A6-Schema-Adherence (verify the §D-1 JSON schema is BNF-v4-clean and the bootstrap_seam gap is fixed)
